title: Alignment & Fine-Tuning (RLHF & LoRA)
description: Transform raw base models into helpful assistants via Instruction Tuning, RLHF, DPO, and Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA).

slides.title: From Base Model to Assistant 🤝
slides.content:
# The Post-Training Pipeline

A raw base model trained on internet text is a document completer, not a chatbot. If you ask: `"What is the capital of France?"`, a base model might simply output: `"What is the capital of Spain? What is the capital of Italy?"`.

### The 3 Stages of Post-Training:
1. **Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT / Instruction Tuning):** Train on high-quality Prompt-Response demonstration pairs (`{"prompt": "What is...", "response": "The capital is Paris."}`).
2. **Preference Alignment (RLHF / DPO):** Humans or AI compare pairs of model outputs. A reward model is trained, and Reinforcement Learning guides the policy towards helpful, harmless, and honest outputs.
3. **Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT / LoRA):** Instead of modifying all 70 billion parameters, **LoRA** injects tiny low-rank decomposition matrices ($A \times B$) into attention weights, training only 0.1% of weights with near-identical performance!

quizData.question: What is the primary operational advantage of Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) for fine-tuning LLMs?

options.text: It converts models into pure C code
It drastically reduces GPU VRAM and storage requirements by training low-rank adapter matrices instead of all base weights
It eliminates the need for any training data
It prevents the model from generating English sentences

quizData.explanation: LoRA freezes the base weights and only trains low-rank adapter matrices, slashing GPU memory consumption and enabling fast adaptation on consumer GPUs.
